column1: # The verdict each tracked counterpart fixture is declared to have, written by
# hand. checks/verify-counterparts.sh scans each tree under
# fixtures/counterparts/ with exactly the rules it applies to a real
# counterpart, and fails if a tree's verdict is not the one declared here.
# This is what stops the rules being useless in either direction. A check that
# passes everything and a check that fails everything are both green on an empty
# set and neither is worth running; one fixture that must pass and three that
# must fail is the cheapest thing that separates them, and it runs on every gate
# rather than on the day somebody remembered to mutate a file.

column3: why this tree has that verdict
every name in it is the package's own; nothing in it is an upstream name and nothing normalizes onto one
a source file names an acquired entry verbatim, which is rule U1 and the branch a transliteration trips first
a source file declares a type whose name is an acquired entry only after case and separator folding, which is rule N1; a transliteration that renames by convention is still a transliteration
